text:
# Founding and Historical Origins

The Spice Bazaar was established in 1660 in Istanbul's Eminonu quarter, built with revenues from the Ottoman eyalet of Egypt -- hence its Turkish name, Misir Carsisi (Egyptian Bazaar). Construction followed the Great Fire of 1660 and was designed by court architect Koca Kasim Aga.

# Architectural Significance

The bazaar forms part of the kulliye (religious complex) of the New Mosque; rent from its shops historically funded the mosque's upkeep. Construction was patronized by Turhan Hatice, the Valide Sultan (Queen Mother) of Sultan Mehmed IV.

# Merchandise and Scale

The bazaar contains around 85 shops selling spices, Turkish delight and other sweets, jewellery, souvenirs, and dried fruits and nuts.

# Position in Istanbul's Shopping Culture

It ranks as the most famous covered shopping complex after the Grand Bazaar, and remains a working spice market as well as a tourist destination.
